review_notes: I read the whole file and the simp-related declarations it depends on. `form_apply` in Basic.lean is `@[simp]` and rewrites `form m x y` to `(x ⬝ᵥ y) / m`, which is a sensible normal form. `signedEquiv_apply` is also `@[simp]`. The file declares only iff and characterisation theorems and no simp lemmas of its own. The `simp [h]` calls use the case hypotheses `u i = 1` and `u i = -1` and rely on existing simp lemmas. I found no competing rules, no rewrite in an unsuitable direction, no credible cycle and no missing canonical simp lemma that the file's uses would need. Adding simp attributes to the `iff` statements would not help, because they are not rewrite-shaped. I could not run Lean, so I did not test simp behaviour. I did not see any practical simp-interface improvement in this file.
